Euro zur Förderung der Herstellung und der Verwertung von Kulturgütern mit österreichischer Prägung in der Form von Fernsehfilmen (einschließlich Fernsehserien, -reihen und -dokumentationen) … zur Verfügung. … 3.6 Mindestlänge (1) Gefördert werden Produktionen mit einer Länge von mindestens 45 Minuten. … (1) Eine Produktion ist nur dann förderungswürdig, wenn sich ein oder mehrere Fernsehveranstalter:innen an der Finanzierung der Produktion mit mindestens 30% an den Gesamtherstellungskosten beteiligen. … 7.1 … (1) Die Herstellung von Produktionen wird grundsätzlich … mit höchstens 20 % der Gesamtherstellungskosten durch nicht rückzahlbare Zuschüsse aus dem FERNSEHFONDS AUSTRIA gefördert. (2) … kann der in Abs. 1 geregelte Prozentsatz um höchstens 2 % erhöht werden. (3) Darüber hinaus kann der Prozentsatz in Ausnahmefällen auf höchstens 28 % der Gesamtherstellungskosten angehoben werden … 9.2 Höhe der Förderungssumme Der Höchstbetrag der Herstellungsförderung sowie der Exzellenzbonusförderung beträgt für fiktionale Produktionen 750.000 Euro dokumentarische Produktionen 550.000 Euro … (1) Die Aufwendungen, die in Österreich umgesetzt werden, sollen mindestens dem 1,6-fachen der gewährten Förderungssumme entsprechen … (2) Insgesamt darf der mit öffentlichen Mitteln geförderte Anteil an den Gesamtherstellungskosten 50 % nicht überschreiten

sources.title: Federal Register of Legislation: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, Volume 7 (Division 376), compilation as at 1 October 2026
sources.said: 376 ‑ 60 Amount of the producer offset The amount of the producer offset is: (a) if the * film is a * feature film that was produced for commercial exhibition to the public in cinemas—40%; or (b) otherwise—30%; of the total of the company’s * qualifying Australian production expenditure on the film … (b) the film is: (i) a * feature film or a film of a like nature; or (ii) a mini ‑ series of television drama; or (iii) a television series that is not covered by subparagraph (i) or (ii); and (c) the film is not, or is not to a substantial extent: … (ii) a film for exhibition as an advertising program or a commercial; or (iii) a film for exhibition as a discussion program, a quiz program, game show, a panel prog … (5) … (i) the series is made up of at least 2 episodes; and (ii) each episode of the series is at least one half of a commercial hour in duration, except where the film is predominantly made using cell, stop motion, digital or other animation, in which case each episode is at least one quarter of a commercial hour in duration … 5 A * film where the application for the certificate is for a series and not for a season of that series, and the series is not a * documentary $1 million $500,000 … 7 A * film where the application for the certificate is for a season of a series, and the series is not a * documentary $1 million $500,000 … (7) The amount worked out for a * film under this subsection is the amount worked out using the formula: where: duration of film in hours means the total length of the * film, measured in hours. total QAPE means the total of the company’s * qualifying Australian production expenditure on the * film … (ii) remuneration provided to the principal director, producers and principal cast associated with the film; to the extent that such expenditure comprises greater than 20% of the company’s * total film expenditure on the film; (c) for a series other than a drama series, or a season of a series other than a drama series—expenditure on an episode beyond the episode in which the 65th commercial hour of the series is reached.

sources.said: filmproductie: een animatiefilm, of een documentairefilm of een speelfilm, al dan niet tot stand gebracht in de vorm van een internationale coproductie, primair bestemd voor bioscoopuitbreng; ... speelfilm: een filmproductie in het genre fictie met een vertoningsduur van tenminste 60 minuten, die primair bestemd is voor bioscoopuitbreng;

sources.title: Netherlands Film Fund: Netherlands Film Production Incentive High-End Series
sources.said: The scheme provides a financial benefit of up to 35% (cash rebate) of the qualifying production costs of national and international high-end drama, documentary and animated series and single episodes that have demonstrably been spent in the Netherlands. … Up to 3 million euros per project per year per applicant production company The grant contribution is a maximum of 35% (cash rebate) of the demonstrably spent qualifying Dutch production costs. … The annual budget for 2026 is € 9,5 million for high-end series, divided across 3 application rounds. … The television/VOD broadcast in the Netherlands is guaranteed. If the TV series is an international co-production, the television/VOD broadcast is guaranteed in two or more countries, including the Netherlands. The series is fully developed from an artistic/content perspective. … A minimum minute price applies as lower limit for the production budget: Documentary series: 4,000 euros per broadcast minute Animated series: 8,000 euros per broadcast minute Drama series for children below the age of 12: a minimum of 10,000 euros in production costs per broadcast minute for a TV series between 10 and 25 minutes per episode, or a minimum of 8,000 euros per broadcast minute for series longer than 25 minutes Drama series (other): 12,000 euros per broadcast minute To be eligible for a financial contribution for a Single Episode the production costs per episode must be a minimum of one million euros. … *Only applicants from the Netherlands, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba can apply for the Film Production Incentive.

sources.title: Federal Register of Legislation: Income Tax Assessment Act 1997, Volume 7 (Division 376), compilation as at 1 October 2026
sources.said: 376 ‑ 60 Amount of the producer offset The amount of the producer offset is: (a) if the * film is a * feature film that was produced for commercial exhibition to the public in cinemas—40%; or (b) otherwise—30%; of the total of the company’s * qualifying Australian production expenditure on the film … (b) the film is: (i) a * feature film or a film of a like nature; or (ii) a mini ‑ series of television drama; or (iii) a television series that is not covered by subparagraph (i) or (ii); and (c) the film is not, or is not to a substantial extent: … (ii) a film for exhibition as an advertising program or a commercial; or (iii) a film for exhibition as a discussion program, a quiz program, game show, a panel prog … (5) … (i) the series is made up of at least 2 episodes; and (ii) each episode of the series is at least one half of a commercial hour in duration, except where the film is predominantly made using cell, stop motion, digital or other animation, in which case each episode is at least one quarter of a commercial hour in duration … 5 A * film where the application for the certificate is for a series and not for a season of that series, and the series is not a * documentary $1 million $500,000 … 7 A * film where the application for the certificate is for a season of a series, and the series is not a * documentary $1 million $500,000 … (7) The amount worked out for a * film under this subsection is the amount worked out using the formula: where: duration of film in hours means the total length of the * film, measured in hours. total QAPE means the total of the company’s * qualifying Australian production expenditure on the * film … (ii) remuneration provided to the principal director, producers and principal cast associated with the film; to the extent that such expenditure comprises greater than 20% of the company’s * total film expenditure on the film; (c) for a series other than a drama series, or a season of a series other than a drama series—expenditure on an episode beyond the episode in which the 65th commercial hour of the series is reached.

sources.title: FFA: German Motion Picture Fund, Richtlinie des BKM (2026)
sources.said: Bei fiktionalen Serien müssen die Gesamtherstellungskosten mindestens 30.000 Euro pro Minute betragen. Satz 1 gilt nicht, wenn die Gesamtherstellungskosten mindestens 1,2 Millionen Euro pro Episode und mindestens 7,2 Millionen Euro pro Staffel betragen. … Bei Serien beträgt die Zuwendung bis zu 30 Prozent der zuwendungsfähigen deutschen Herstellungskosten, höchstens jedoch 6 Millionen Euro pro Staffel. … 7,2 Millionen Euro bei fiktionalen Serien mit deutschen Herstellungskosten von bis zu 32 Millionen Euro, … 10,5 Millionen Euro bei fiktionalen Serien mit deutschen Herstellungskosten von bis zu 40 Millionen Euro, … 20 Millionen Euro bei fiktionalen Serien mit deutschen Herstellungskosten von mehr als 40 Millionen Euro. … Bemessungssgrundlage für die Höhe der Zuwendung sind die deutschen Herstellungskosten, höchstens jedoch 80 Prozent der Gesamtherstellungskosten. … (1) Diese Richtlinie tritt am 01.01.2026 in Kraft und ist befristet bis 31.12.2026.

sources.title: FFA: German Motion Picture Fund (GMPF)
sources.said: Der German Motion Picture Fund – ein Förderprogramm des Beauftragten der Bundesregierung für Kultur und Medien (BKM) – unterstützt die Produktion hochbudgetierter Serien und Filme, die nicht im Kino ausgewertet werden. … Ab 2025 wird die Förderung bei Vorliegen aller Fördervoraussetzungen als nichtrückzahlbarer Zuschuss in Höhe von bis zu 30 Prozent der zuwendungsfähigen deutschen Kosten vergeben. … Ab sofort ist eine Antragsannahme für Projekte mit Drehbeginn im Jahr 2026 nicht mehr möglich. Das vorgesehene Antragsvolumen von 30 Mio. Euro wurde erreicht

sources.title: Umsatzsteuergesetz (UStG) § 4 Steuerbefreiungen bei Lieferungen und sonstigen Leistungen, Nr. 20 (gesetze-im-internet.de, Bundesministerium der Justiz)
sources.said: 20. a) die Umsätze folgender Einrichtungen juristischer Personen des öffentlichen Rechts: Theater, Orchester, Kammermusikensembles, Chöre, Museen, … Das Gleiche gilt für die Umsätze gleichartiger Einrichtungen anderer Unternehmer, wenn die zuständige Landesbehörde bescheinigt, dass sie die gleichen kulturellen Aufgaben wie die in Satz 1 bezeichneten Einrichtungen erfüllen. Steuerfrei sind auch die Umsätze von Bühnenregisseuren und Bühnenchoreographen an Einrichtungen im Sinne der Sätze 1 und 2, wenn die zuständige Landesbehörde bescheinigt, dass deren künstlerische Leistungen diesen Einrichtungen unmittelbar dienen. … b) die Veranstaltung von Theatervorführungen und Konzerten durch andere Unternehmer, wenn die Darbietungen von den unter Buchstabe a bezeichneten Theatern, Orchestern, Kammermusikensembles oder Chören erbracht werden,

sources.title: Umsatzsteuergesetz (UStG) § 12 Steuersätze (gesetze-im-internet.de)
sources.said: (1) Die Steuer beträgt für jeden steuerpflichtigen Umsatz 19 Prozent der Bemessungsgrundlage … (2) Die Steuer ermäßigt sich auf sieben Prozent für die folgenden Umsätze: … 7. a) die Eintrittsberechtigung für Theater, Konzerte und Museen, sowie die den Theatervorführungen und Konzerten vergleichbaren Darbietungen ausübender Künstler

Germany's theatre tax treatment found is in VAT: an exemption for public (and certified private) theatres and for certified stage directors' fees, and the reduced 7% rate on theatre admission. No production tax credit for a play was met; the Income and Corporation Tax Acts were not read whole, so no absence of one is stated. The engine would read the exemption as a cost a public-theatre production does not carry and the 7% as the ticket tax a private run pays. | stage.fund: The fund publishes how many it funded per round, not how many applied, so no rate of yes. Public theatres are funded by Länder and towns, not by project. | stage.outcomes: Not searched (the Bühnenverein's Theaterstatistik is sold, not published). German public theatre plays in repertoire on subsidy (earned income covers 15.9% of costs), so a run is not recouped: a play sells a share of its seats (70.3% in Schauspiel, 2023/24) at €36.20 earned per visit on average, against €191.27 of subsidy per visit. No count of runs recouping or extended exists in either publication read; the private theatres' chapter (3) holds visits and performances by house, not by run. Box office per performance is not printed; earned income per visit is.

sources.title: Agency for Culture and Palaces: Guidelines for applying for support under the Live Action Scheme (August 2026)
sources.said: The Live Action Scheme: a scheme for feature films, fiction series, documentary films and documentary series with an annual budget of DKK 100 million. … 2. Fiction series must have: • a total budget of DKK 150,000 per minute and a total budget of at least DKK 15 million per season of the fiction series, • and eligible costs of at least DKK 3 million. … A fiction series means a series with a fictional, interconnected narrative, divided into a number of related episodes, with either self-contained or continuous storylines. Several related episodes are referred to as a season. … The scheme is structured as a rebate scheme under which 25 per cent of the eligible expenditure incurred in Denmark for the production may be reimbursed … Please also note that a maximum grant of DKK 20 million may be awarded

sources.title: DGCINE: Ley No. 108-10 para el Fomento de la Actividad Cinematográfica (text as amended by Ley 82-13), from its Marco Legal page
sources.said: Párrafo III.-En adición a las obras cinematográficas, podrán acogerse a los incentivos fiscales de la presente ley las siguientes obras audiovisuales: películas para televisión, series y miniseries de televisión para distribución nacional o internacional, documentales, telenovelas y videos musicales. Estas obras audiovisuales deberán contar con una calificación previa de la DGCINE … Artículo 39. Crédito Fiscal Transferible (Modificado por la Ley No. 82-13 de fecha 27 de junio de 2013 …). Podrán optar por beneficiarse de un crédito fiscal equivalente a un veinticinco (25%) de todos los gastos realizados en la República Dominicana, las personas naturales o jurídicas que produzcan obras cinematográficas y audiovisuales dominicanas o extranjeras en el territorio dominicano. … Párrafo II.- El crédito fiscal podrá ser solicitado respecto a presupuestos ejecutados parcial o totalmente, siempre y cuando el monto de los gastos realizados al momento de la solicitud sea igual o mayor a la suma de quinientos mil dólares (US$500,000.00).

sources.title: Decreto No. 370-11, Reglamento de Aplicación de la Ley No. 108-10 (G. O. No. 10623, 28 June 2011), DGCINE's Marco Legal copy
sources.said: Artículo 168.- Gastos Excluidos. Quedan excluidos de la aplicación del Artículo 39 de la Ley No. 108-10 los siguientes gastos: a) La proporción de los gastos por concepto de honorarios del productor que exceda el 6% del presupuesto total de la producción de la obra. b) La proporción de los gastos de desarrollo que exceda el 3% del presupuesto total de la producción de la obra. c) Cargos financieros y gastos por concepto de fianzas o garantías de fiel cumplimiento. d) Costos relacionados al mercadeo y distribución de la obra.

sources.title: BOE consolidated text: Ley 27/2014 del Impuesto sobre Sociedades, art. 36 (última actualización publicada el 28/12/2022, en vigor a partir del 29/12/2022)
sources.said: 1. Las inversiones en producciones españolas de largometrajes y cortometrajes cinematográficos y de series audiovisuales de ficción, animación o documental, que permitan la confección de un soporte físico previo a su producción industrial seriada darán derecho al productor o a los contribuyentes que participen en la financiación a una deducción: a) Del 30 por ciento respecto del primer millón de base de la deducción. b) Del 25 por ciento sobre el exceso de dicho importe. … Al menos el 50 por ciento de la base de la deducción deberá corresponderse con gastos realizados en territorio español. El importe de esta deducción no podrá ser superior a 20 millones de euros. En el caso de series audiovisuales, la deducción se determinará por episodio y el límite a que se refiere el párrafo anterior será de 10 millones de euros por cada episodio producido. … El importe de esta deducción, conjuntamente con el resto de ayudas percibidas, no podrá superar el 50 por ciento del coste de producción. … 2. … La deducción se aplicará siempre que los gastos realizados en territorio español sean, al menos, de 1 millón de euros. … En el caso de series audiovisuales, la deducción se determinará por episodio y el límite a que se refiere el párrafo anterior será de 10 millones de euros por cada episodio producido. … Se modifican los apartados 1 y 2, con efectos para los períodos impositivos que se inicien a partir de 1 de enero de 2023, por la disposición final 5.2 de la Ley 38/2022

sources.said: The production incentive in Finland is a maximum of 25% cash rebate for production costs. ... The budget for the audiovisual production incentive for 2026 is 10 million euros. ... sources.said: § 1. 1) Fyri filmar, sendirøðir og heimildarfilmar, sum verða framleidd í Føroyum, verða 25% av útreiðslunum, sum eru hildnar í Føroyum, afturbornar, um umsøkjarin lýkur treytirnar fyri at fáa afturbering. sources.title: CNC: Crédit d'impôt audiovisuel
sources.said: Fiction Durée supérieure ou égale à 45 minutes ; Conditions de coût : coût global de production supérieur ou égal à 5 000 € par minute produite … Taux de crédit d’impôt fixé à 25% (décret 2016-52 du 27 janvier 2016 - article 77 de la loi n° 2014-1655) ; Plafonds déductibles : Suite à la parution du décret n° 2016-1191 du 31 août 2016, les plafonds pour les œuvres audiovisuelles de fiction ont été modifiés. La somme des crédits d'impôt calculés au titre d'une même œuvre audiovisuelle de fiction ne peut excéder : 1 250 € par minute produite et livrée lorsque le coût de production est inférieur à 10 000 € par minute produite et livrée 1 500 € par minute produite et livrée lorsque le coût de production est supérieur ou égal à 10 000 € et inférieur à 15 000 € par minute produite et livrée 2 000 € par minute produite et livrée lorsque le coût de production est supérieur ou égal à 15 000 € et inférieur à 20 000 € par minute produite et livrée 3 000 € par minute produite et livrée lorsque le coût de production est supérieur ou égal à 20 000 € et inférieur à 25 000 € par minute produite et livrée 4 000 € par minute produite et livrée lorsque le coût de production est supérieur ou égal à 25 000 € et inférieur à 30 000 € par minute produite et livrée 5 000 € par minute produite et livrée lorsque le coût de production est supérieur ou égal à 30 000 € et inférieur à 35 000 € par minute produite et livrée 7 500 € par minute produite et livrée lorsque le coût de production est supérieur ou égal à 35 000 € et inférieur à 40 000 € par minute produite et livrée 10 000 € par minute produite et livrée lorsque le coût de production est supérieur ou égal à 40 000 € par minute produite et livrée

sources.title: CNC: Fiction – aide sélective à la production (Fonds de soutien audiovisuel)
sources.said: Les entreprises (ou associations) ne disposant pas d’un compte automatique, pour être éligibles : … doivent être indépendantes de tout éditeur de services de télévision … Les œuvres doivent faire l’objet d’un apport initial sous forme de préachat des droits de diffusion complété éventuellement d’un apport en coproduction , explicitée par un contrat : D’un ou plusieurs diffuseurs français … Le financement des œuvres doit contenir une part française correspondant au moins à 30% de leur coût définitif et faire l’objet de dépenses de production en France pour au moins 50% de cette part française. … L’ensemble des aides accordées par le Fonds de soutien audiovisuel ne peut excéder 40% du coût définitif de l’œuvre (ou de la part française en cas de coproduction internationale). Le montant total des aides accordées par l’Etat, l’un de ses établissements et les collectivités locales ne peut dépasser 50% du coût définitif de l’œuvre

sources.title: CNC: Fiction – compte automatique, aide à la production
sources.said: Les œuvres bénéficiant d'un apport d'un ou de diffuseurs français au moins égal à 25% de la part française du financement, et composé d'une part de numéraire supérieure à 12 000 € de l'heure. Les œuvres dont le financement en numéraire par un diffuseur est inférieur à 12 000 € de l'heure mais bénéficiant d'un avis favorable de la commission sélective du FSA. … En fiction, le producteur obtiendra l'ouverture d'un compte automatique s'il atteint au moins le seuil suivant : 200 000 €.

sources.title: HKSAR Government press release, 14 May 2026: Results of final winners of Content Development Scheme for Streaming Platforms announced (issued for the FDC)
sources.said: Four final winners of the Content Development Scheme for Streaming Platforms under the Film Development Fund (FDF) have been selected. Each winner will receive a maximum of $4.5 million for the production of a pilot of their streaming series. … The Scheme, having received over 50 eligible applications, recruited participating teams through a competition to develop content for a series for streaming platforms. Among the applications, 10 projects were shortlisted, and each received a script development fee of $600,000 to $1.2 million to develop a full production proposal and scripts of an entire series. The final four winners out of the 10 shortlisted projects each receive a maximum of $4.5 million to produce a pilot of the series to identify potential platform investors. Together with the script development fee, each final winning team is awarded a total of up to $5.7 million.

sources.title: FDC: Content Development Scheme for Streaming Platforms – Guide to Application
sources.said: 4.1 … (b) each and every producer, director, script supervisor and scriptwriter must be a permanent resident of Hong Kong aged eighteen (18) years or above; … 4.2 The proposed mini-series (“Mini-series”) shall have at least six (6) episodes, with the running time of each episode of at least forty-five (45) minutes. It shall be a fictional narrative (animated series and docuseries not included). … 6.3.3 … ten (10) Applications as Phase 2 projects … will receive a cash prize of a minimum of $600,000 for a six (6)-episode Mini-series, with $100,000 for each episode from the 7th episode up to $1,200,000 being the maximum amount … 6.4.2 … not more than four (4) Mini-series (“Phase 3 Projects”) will be selected. … will receive a cash prize of $4.5 million for producing the Pilot Episodes. … the cash prize shall only be used for production of the Pilot Episodes and shall not cover any other expenses such as promotion and marketing, distribution etc. … 6.5.5 … it can of its own volition seek funding from other investors, financiers and/or streaming platform operators to finance the production of the remaining episodes of the Mini-series. Unless with the approval of the Government, the completed entire series can only be released on streaming platforms which are on the list of streaming platforms to be specified by the Government from time to time and are available to viewers in Hong Kong within the first three (3) years upon the completion of the Pilot Episodes. If the Selected Phase 2 Company secures funding to finance the completion of the entire Mini-series, the entire series shall only be available on streaming platforms on a subscription basis in the first year of release.

sources.title: National Film Institute Hungary: Hungarian Film Incentive
sources.said: Films (for cinema and television) produced in Hungary are eligible for a 30% rebate based on their expenditure (all the direct film production costs) spent in the country. … The 30% incentive is extendable to 37.5% of the eligible production expense by adding 7.5% non-Hungarian costs. sources.title: Jerusalem Film Fund (Jerusalem Development Authority): Large-Budget International Productions
sources.said: “Television Series” – A fiction series with at least 7 episodes, each episode at least 24 minutes in length. “An International Production” – A production of a Film or a Television Series, with the main funding from abroad. The producer and production company are legally registered abroad ... The main spoken language in the Film or TV series is not an official language in Israel. ... a.The Production Budget in Israel shall be no less than NIS 8 million. ... d. The Budget Referred to Jerusalem shall be no less than 25% of the total Production Budget in Israel and no less than NIS 2 million. e. The Production has distribution agreements, according to which the Film or Series shall be broadcast in territories where there are at least 80 million residents. ... The Fund's support shall be a return of 60% of the Budget Referred to Jerusalem, and in any case shall not exceed NIS10,000,000 ... the amount of the grant shall not exceed 50% of the total Production's Budget Referred to Israel.

sources.title: Kvikmyndamiðstöð Íslands: Framleiðslustyrkir
sources.said: Framleiðslustyrkir eru veittir til leikinna kvikmynda, stuttmynda, heimildamynda og leikins sjónvarpsefnis Tímabundin vilyrði og framleiðslustyrkir eru aðeins veittir íslenskum framleiðslufyrirtækjum sem hafa kvikmyndagerð að meginstarfi. … Skilyrði fyrir framleiðslustyrk er að fyrir liggi skriflegir samningar eða staðfestingar um að fjármögnun sé að fullu lokið hjá öðrum en Kvikmyndasjóði. Við úthlutun á framleiðslustyrkjum til leikins sjónvarpsefnis er horft til fjárhagslegrar þátttöku sjónvarpsstöðvar í formi greiðslu fyrir sýningarrétt. … Leiknar kvikmyndir, sjónvarpsefni og stuttmyndir Hámarksupphæð Fer eftir umfangi verkefnis. … Vilyrði fyrir sýningu í sjónvarpi. … Í tilfellum þegar verkefnið er fyrsta eða önnur mynd leikstjóra er krafa um að reyndur framleiðandi komi að verkefninu. … Reyndur framleiðandi er framleiðandi sem hefur verið aðalframleiðandi a.m.k. tveggja kvikmyndaverka … eða tveggja sjónvarpsþáttaraða sem hafa verið sýndar í sjónvarpi.

Þóknun framleiðenda skal vera í samræmi við eðli og umfang verkefnis og er háð samþykki Kvikmyndamiðstöðvar. … Þóknun framleiðenda  Sé hlutfallið yfir 7,5% af heildarkostnaði þarf að rökstyðja það sérstaklega, t.d. vegna verkefna með lítilli veltu en verulegri vinnu í undirbúningi. … Markaðs- og kynningarkostnaður telst almennt ekki til framleiðslukostnaðar kvikmyndar eða sjónvarpsefnis.

sources.title: Закон КР от 2 октября 2001 года № 86 «О государственной поддержке кинематографии Кыргызской Республики», редакция от 21.02.2018 (Centralized Data Bank of Legal Information, Ministry of Justice; API GetEdition?editionId=865154)
sources.said: Статья 3 ... Фильм - киноаудиовидеопроизведение, созданное в художественной, хроникально-документальной, научно-популярной, учебной, анимационной, телевизионной или иной форме ... Статья 8. ... Формами государственной поддержки кинематографии являются: ... полное государственное финансирование государственных заказов и кинолетописи; частичное государственное финансирование производства, тиражирования, проката и показа национальных фильмов; льготное валютное и иное финансовое регулирование деятельности организаций кинематографии. ... Статья 9. ... Государственное финансирование кинематографии устанавливается в размере не менее 0,1 процента расходной части республиканского бюджета на соответствующий финансовый год. ... Статья 10. ... принимает решение о выделении организации кинематографии, продюсеру средств на производство национального фильма с учетом мнения экспертных комиссий ... Государственное финансирование производства национального фильма обеспечивается в размере не ниже 51 процента сметной стоимости его производства. В исключительных случаях ... до 100 процентов сметной стоимости его производства.

sources.title: Указ Президента КР от 20 мая 2022 года УП № 159 «О мерах по развитию национальной киноиндустрии и дальнейшему совершенствованию системы государственной поддержки кинематографии Кыргызской Республики» (CBD, GetEdition?editionId=1169159)
sources.said: 2. Определить приоритетными направлениями развития национальной кинематографии: - финансовое обеспечение производства национальных кинофильмов, сериалов, анимационных фильмов; ... при Департаменте кинематографии при Министерстве культуры, информации, спорта и молодежной политики Кыргызской Республики (далее - государственное учреждение "Творческо-производственное объединение "Кыргызсериал"); - Фонда кино.

Series are a stated priority of state film financing (Decree 159), and the state makes its own series through Kyrgyzserial; whether an independent producer's series may draw the 51% state share, and how often one is funded, was not found. The Film Fund's regulation was not found in the CBD in the time given. | stage.outcomes: Kyrgyzstan: state budget funds national films (producer-KG.json). Not attempted today. sources.title: 방송법 제72조(순수외주제작 방송프로그램의 편성) [시행 2026. 4. 21.] [법률 제21572호]
sources.said: ①방송사업자는 해당 채널의 전체 방송프로그램중 국내에서 해당 방송사업자나 그 특수관계자가 아닌 자가 제작한 방송프로그램(이하 “순수외주제작 방송프로그램”이라 한다)을 대통령령 으로 정하는 바에 따라 일정한 비율 이상 편성하여야 한다.

sources.title: 방송법 시행령 제58조 [시행 2026. 10. 16.] [대통령령 제36687호]
sources.said: 텔레비전방송프로그램(영화는 제외하며, 이하 “순수외주제작 방송프로그램”이라 한다)을 해당 채널의 매반기 전체 텔레비전방송시간의 100분의 35 이내에서 방송미디어통신위원회가 정하여 고시하는 비율 이상 편성하여야 한다. … 매반기 주시청시간대 텔레비전방송시간의 100분의 15 이내에서 방송미디어통신위원회가 고시하는 비율 이상

sources.title: 방송프로그램 등의 편성에 관한 고시 [시행 2026. 6. 30.] [방송미디어통신위원회고시 제2026-20호] (body read from admRulLsInfoR.do)
sources.said: 1. 한국방송공사. 가. 지상파제1텔레비전방송: 해당 채널별 매반기 전체 텔레비전 방송시간의 100분의 19 이상 나. 지상파제2텔레비전방송: 해당 채널별 매반기 전체 텔레비전 방송시간의 100분의 35 이상 2. 「방송문화진흥회법」 에 따른 방송문화진흥회가 최다출자자인 지상파방송사업자. 가. 지상파텔레비전방송: 해당 채널별 매반기 전체 텔레비전 방송시간의 100분의 30 이상 … 4. … 직전 3개 사업연도 평균 매출액이 3천억원 이상인 지상파방송사업자. 가. 지상파텔레비전방송: 해당 채널별 매반기 전체 텔레비전 방송시간의 100분의 30 이상 5. 한국교육방송공사: … 100분의 16 이상 … 7. 종합편성을 행하는 방송채널사용사업자 : 해당 채널별 매반기 전체 텔레비전 방송시간의 100분의 30 이상 ② … 매반기 주시청시간대 텔레비전 방송시간의 100분의 10 이상 … 제9조의2 … 다음 각 호 중 3가지 이상의 요건을 갖추고 외주제작사가 실질적인 제작을 담당한 방송프로그램 … 1. 외주제작사가 작가 … 와의 계약 체결을 담당하는 경우 2. 외주제작사가 주요 출연자와의 계약 체결을 담당하는 경우 3. 외주제작사가 주요 스태프 … 중 2가지 이상 분야의 책임자와의 계약 체결을 담당하는 경우 4. 외주제작사가 방송프로그램 제작에 소요되는 재원의 100분의 30 이상을 조달하는 경우 5. 외주제작사가 제작비의 집행 및 관리와 관련된 제반 의사 결정을 담당하는 경우 … ⑦ … 외주제작사가 저작권 전부를 보유하는 조항이 있을 경우에는 편성시간의 100분의 130으로 인정한다.

sources.title: Lithuanian Film Centre: Tax Incentive, How it Works
sources.said: From 2019 Lithuanian Film Tax Incentive offers an opportunity to save up to 30% of the film production budget through private investment scheme. … The incentive is available for the production of feature films, TV dramas, documentaries and animated films. It includes domestically produced, co-produced or commissioned films (produced under the service agreement). At least 80% of eligible film production costs must be incurred in Lithuania and the total amount of eligible spend in Lithuania has to be no less than 43,000 EUR. … Payment for actors (if the payment exceeds 4% of the production costs of the film or its part). … A film is not considered to meet the criteria for cultural content evaluation if: It is an advertisement, promotional video, television program, reality show, lifestyle show, music video, video game, or a series characterized by certain character archetypes and dramaturgical rules that allow for infinite continuation without creating artistic value … At least three days of shooting take place in Lithuania … At least 51% of the crew hired by the Lithuanian production company are citizens of Lithuania or citizens of other European Economic Area (EEA) countries.

sources.title: Collectivité de Saint-Martin: Résidence fiscale à Saint-Martin - La règle des 5 ans
sources.said: Saint-Martin dispose d'une fiscalité propre, distincte de celle de la métropole et des DOM. Pour bénéficier du régime fiscal saint-martinois, il ne suffit pas d'y résider : des règles spécifiques de domiciliation fiscale s'appliquent, notamment la règle dite « des cinq ans » pour les personnes venant de l'hexagone ou d'un département d'outre mer (DOM).

sources.title: Collectivité de Saint-Martin: Règlement du Fonds d'aides territorial à la filière audiovisuelle et cinéma, 4. Aide sélective à la production d'œuvres audiovisuelles
sources.said: Les sociétés constituées sous forme commerciale dont l’objet principal est la production et établie en France, dans l’Union européenne ou dans l’Espace économique européen, si elle dispose d’un établissement stable en France, au moment du versement de l’aide … Les projets disposant déjà d’un accord de diffusion (service de télévision ou service de médias audiovisuels à la demande). La Collectivité de Saint-Martin attribue une aide selon les modalités suivantes: 50% des dépenses éligibles, plafonnée à 120 000€ ; - Série de courte durée (inférieure ou égale à 26 minutes) : 60 % des dépenses éligibles, plafonnée à 40 000 € ; - Série de longue durée (52’ minutes ou plus) : 60 % des dépenses éligibles, plafonnée à 120 000 €. … Le montant total des aides publiques ne peut excéder 50% du coût définitif de l’œuvre … Le seuil d’intensité peut s’élever à 60 % pour les œuvres difficiles ou à petit budget … une œuvre à petit budget est celle dont le budget total est inférieur ou égal à cent mille euros (100 000 €) par heure. … Les dépenses éligibles pour cette aide sont les suivantes : - Salaires et charges des techniciens, - Frais de location, - Frais de déplacements … - Lieux de tournage, - Coûts liés à l’achat et la fabrication de décors, - Frais de post-production

sources.title: Netherlands Film Fund: Netherlands Film Production Incentive High-End Series
sources.said: The scheme provides a financial benefit of up to 35% (cash rebate) of the qualifying production costs of national and international high-end drama, documentary and animated series and single episodes that have demonstrably been spent in the Netherlands. … Up to 3 million euros per project per year per applicant production company The grant contribution is a maximum of 35% (cash rebate) of the demonstrably spent qualifying Dutch production costs. … The annual budget for 2026 is € 9,5 million for high-end series, divided across 3 application rounds. … The television/VOD broadcast in the Netherlands is guaranteed. If the TV series is an international co-production, the television/VOD broadcast is guaranteed in two or more countries, including the Netherlands. The series is fully developed from an artistic/content perspective. … A minimum minute price applies as lower limit for the production budget: Documentary series: 4,000 euros per broadcast minute Animated series: 8,000 euros per broadcast minute Drama series for children below the age of 12: a minimum of 10,000 euros in production costs per broadcast minute for a TV series between 10 and 25 minutes per episode, or a minimum of 8,000 euros per broadcast minute for series longer than 25 minutes Drama series (other): 12,000 euros per broadcast minute To be eligible for a financial contribution for a Single Episode the production costs per episode must be a minimum of one million euros. … *Only applicants from the Netherlands, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba can apply for the Film Production Incentive.

sources.title: NFI: Insentivordningen
sources.said: Du kan søke om å få refundert inntil 25 % av godkjente produksjonskostnader for produksjonen i Norge. Vi kan gi refusjon til produksjon av spillefilm, dokumentarfilm- og serier og dramaserier som er produsert helt eller delvis i Norge. Du kan søke med flere sesonger i en serie til samme søknadsrunde forutsatt at det leveres en søknad per sesong. ... Produksjonen må minimum ha et totalt produksjonsbudsjett på: 25.000.000 kroner for spillefilm ... 10.000.000 kroner per episode for dramaserie 5.000.000 kroner per episode for dokumentarserie Produksjonen må ha et budsjett som viser et minimumsforbruk av godkjente kostnader i Norge på 4.000.000 kroner. ... Refusjonsramme tildeles prosjektene i tråd med rangeringen og i henhold til budsjettet for søknadsrunden.

sources.title: NFI: Produksjon av dramaserie etter kunstnerisk vurdering
sources.said: Søkeren skal være et uavhengig produksjonsselskap som er etablert i Norge eller i et annet EØS-land ... du må ha inngått en forpliktende avtale med en visningsplattform om vesentlig finansiering av prosjektet. ... Søknaden må normalt gjelde en fiksjonsbasert dramaserie (ett verk), som minimum består av tre episoder med lengde på minimum én kommersiell halvtime. ... Samlet tilskudd fra Norsk filminstitutt til utvikling og produksjon kan maksimalt være 35.000.000 kroner. Det maksimale samlede offentlige tilskuddet skal ikke overstige 50% av de godkjente regnskapsførte utviklings-, produksjons- og lanseringskostnadene. ... Visningsplattformen må være tilgjengelig for alle i Norge, og ha en bred markedsandel i Norge.

sources.title: Ley 16 de 2012 (G.O. 27,024-C), Ministerio de Cultura / Dirección Nacional de Cine copy, art. 45
sources.said: Artículo 45. Incentivo económico. La empresa extranjera que al amparo de esta Ley realice una obra cinematográfica o audiovisual gozará de un retorno económico del 15% del total de sus compras de bienes y servicios debidamente documentados y pagados a favor de proveedores nacionales ubicados dentro del territorio panameño. Quedan excluidas de dicho retorno las compras de bienes o servicios efectuados a profesionales y/o talentos que no sean de nacionalidad panameña. El retorno será otorgado por el Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias a las empresas cuyos costos o gastos de producciones realizadas dentro del territorio panameño sean mayores a tres millones de balboas (B/.3,000,000.00), hasta un máximo de cuarenta millones de balboas (B/.40,000,000.00).

I/2027's final results were not yet published (only the administrative check: 138 rows). | stage.outcomes: Not reached. A single public theatre's own report, not a national count: ticket revenue covers every event the theatre ran (220 actions including hosted ones), so revenue per own performance (592,541 / 87) overstates what one own performance takes. Tickets cover about 3.5% of the theatre's approved revenue (the county budget pays the rest), so 'recouping' is not how a Romanian public theatre's play fares. sources.said: Søkeren skal være et uavhengig produksjonsselskap som er etablert i Norge eller i et annet EØS-land … Foretaket må være organisert som aksjeselskap og være registrert i det norske enhets- eller foretaksregisteret. … Samlet tilskudd fra Norsk filminstitutt til utvikling og produksjon kan maksimalt være 35.000.000 kroner. sources.title: Innst. 383 S (2024–2025), familie- og kulturkomiteen
sources.said: viser til at Svalbardloven § 2 annet ledd slår fast at offentligrettslige reguleringer utover strafferett og rettergangslovgivning ikke gjelder på Svalbard, med mindre det er særskilt fastsatt. Siden det ikke er fastsatt i Norsk filminstitutts (NFI) forskrifter at de skal gjelde for Svalbard, følger det av Svalbardloven § 2 at de ikke gjelder der. … «Stortinget ber regjeringen endre virkeområdet for Norsk filminstitutts relevante forskrifter om støtte til film- og serieproduksjon til også å omfatte Svalbard, slik at kostnader påløpt på Svalbard regnes som kostnader påløpt i Norge.»

Le imprese dell’industria audiovisiva, nazionali od estere con stabile organizzazione in territorio, che realizzano a San Marino in tutto o in parte progetti cinematografici, audiovisivi o teatrali godono delle seguenti agevolazioni fiscali: a) abbattimento del reddito imponibile pari al 50% dei costi sostenuti in territorio riconducibili ad ogni singola produzione; b) riduzione dell’aliquota monofase ordinaria pari al 50%, fatta salva l’applicazione delle aliquote vigenti sui beni strumentali. 2. In aggiunta ai benefici di cui al comma 1, le imprese ivi indicate hanno diritto ad uno sgravio contributivo sino ad un massimo del 20% per ogni lavoratore assunto in esecuzione a piani occupazionali approvati dalla Segreteria di Stato per il Lavoro. … Il beneficio di cui al comma 2 non può eccedere i 24 mesi a decorrere dal momento dell’assunzione. Art. 15 … 1. Le donazioni di privati o di imprese, enti, banche, fondazioni, associazioni, effettuate a favore e a sostegno delle produzioni cinematografiche alle quali venga riconosciuto un valore aggiunto per la promozione della cultura, dei luoghi e del turismo o dello Stato, sono interamente deducibili ai fini della determinazione del reddito imponibile. 2. Le produzioni di cui al comma 1 sono individuate mediante delibera del Congresso di Stato.

sources.title: Legge 27 giugno 2013 n.71, Legge in materia di sostegno allo sviluppo economico, art. 37
sources.said: Art. 37 (Sviluppo ed implementazione del settore audio-visivo) 1. In un’ottica di sviluppo e di implementazione della competitività e redditività della produzione, commercializzazione, distribuzione e vendita dei prodotti dell’industria audio- visiva, il Congresso di Stato adotta apposito decreto delegato, che disciplina organicamente il settore suddetto, secondo le prassi e gli standard normativi internazionali in materia.

sources.said: “1. Per le erogazioni liberali in denaro effettuate nei periodi d’imposta per interventi di manutenzione, protezione e restauro di beni culturali pubblici, … manutenzione dei teatri, sostegno alle istituzioni concertistiche, … eventi culturali, patrocinati dalla Segreteria di Stato per la Cultura e con delibera del Congresso di Stato, … dichiarati eventi di “rilevanza culturale”; iniziative editoriali, progetti audiovisivi e multimediali, patrocinati dalla Segreteria di Stato per la Cultura e con delibera del Congresso di Stato, … dichiarati eventi di “rilevanza culturale”; … si applica la piena deducibilità dell’importo erogato e spetta un credito d’imposta, nella misura del 65% delle erogazioni effettuate fino ad un massimo di complessivi euro 100.000,00 (centomila/00) da ripartire in tre quote annuali di pari importo. 2. foundInPart: series.incentive: San Marino: not attempted today. Read whole on the Consiglio Grande e Generale archive (a PDF served under a .html address). A series is not named, but it is an 'audiovisual project'. There is no threshold or cap. Whether art. 14 was later amended or repealed was not settled: the archive's content search does not index this decree's text, and it is marked TESTI COORDINATI. The Finance Commission's order of the day of 22 January 2025 asked the government to 'evaluate a specific tax regime for audiovisual productions'. That shows no further regime was in force then. It does not show that art. 14 lapsed. | series.fund: San Marino: not attempted today. No dedicated screen fund was found (the Film Commission was still being proposed in January 2025). The Fondo sammarinese per la Cultura (L.167/2022, EUR 20,000 endowment) serves heritage and public cultural places. | series.outcomes: San Marino: not attempted today. Its site publishes no commissioning terms or calls for independent producers (Chi siamo and Azienda were read). The January 2025 order of the day also asks for a new seat for San Marino RTV and for joining the co-production convention. | stage.incentive: San Marino: not attempted today. DD 63/2014 names theatre projects. The amendment caveat of item 1 holds. The Art Bonus helps a play only once it is patronised and declared an event of cultural relevance. | stage.fund: San Marino: not attempted today. A general events contribution, not a theatre fund. No amounts or approvals were found: the Secretariats publish only the small grants, and their sites were not reached (gov.sm reset on 2026-11-01). Whether DD 27/2014 was later amended was not checked.

sources.title: FOPICA: Documentaires & séries
sources.said: Documentaires (>60 min cinéma ou 52 min TV), séries, feuilletons et collections. 75 M FCFA Ce dispositif soutient la production d'œuvres documentaires de création (plus de 60 minutes pour le cinéma, 52 minutes pour la télévision) ainsi que les séries, feuilletons et collections. **Plafond d'intervention :** jusqu'à 75 millions FCFA par projet. **Modalités de versement** (convention 24 mois) : - 20 % à la signature de la convention ; - 50 % au démarrage du tournage ; - 20 % au démarrage de la postproduction ; - 10 % à la livraison. **Exclusions :** captations, talkshows, magazines, reportages télévisuels, émissions de flux, sitcoms, clips musicaux, films institutionnels et/ou didactiques, publicités.

sources.title: Rijkscultuurfondsen.org (the national cultural funds' guide for the ABCSSS islands): Production Subsidy (Performing Arts Fund NL)
sources.said: The Production Subsidy is aimed at organisations whose primary purpose is to develop, perform or re-enact professional performances, concerts or competitions. The organisation must have produced at least two professional productions or the creators must have been active as professional performing artists for at least two years . … It is possible to apply for production grants up to a maximum of 78,750 euros. However, if you are applying for a production grant for more new compositions, librettos or theatrical texts an additional grant of up to 26,250 euros is available. … There are three application rounds a year. … Your budget must meet the standard of 20% of total budget must come from your own income … Your organisation’s aim must be the production of professional performing arts and it must have legal personality … The premiere date must be at least four months after the deadline for the application round

foundInPart: series.incentive: thailandfilmoffice.go.th: CONNECT tunnel 502. A Thai producer's own series has no incentive found. | series.outcomes: Not read. Per-episode figures are division of the stated totals (arithmetic). Thai PBS's published notices give prices, not a tariff or a rate of acceptance; the open-call notices (ประกาศคัดสรร) and their terms were listed but not read. The commercial broadcasters' commissioning is not public. The scriptwriter award is also a Thai series-writer fee data point (writer-TH). | stage.fund: Not searched. 44 projects across all nine branches in FY2569 (not the performing-arts count). The 200,000 baht figure is the ceiling a project may have for the OCAC director to approve it alone, not a grant ceiling. Applications and their count are not published on the pages read, so no rate of yes. The handbook is undated (it cites a FY2561 project). The site is script-rendered (Inertia); its embedded page data was read.

sources.title: Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığı Sinema Genel Müdürlüğü: Yabancı Film Yapım Desteği
sources.said: Destek tutarı, ülke içinde harcanan ve Bakanlıkça kabul edilen tutarın %30’unu aşamaz. … (100 puan üzerinden en az 50 puan alınmalıdır.) … Türlere göre Türkiye’de harcanması gereken en az tutarlar aşağıdaki gibidir. … Belgesel 8 milyon TL Dizi (bölüm başına) 13 milyon TL … Desteklenen yapımın ticari amaçla sinema salonu, kablo, uydu, karasal ve internet ortamlarından en az birinde yurtdışı gösterimi zorunludur. … Yabancı Film Yapım Desteği Başvurular yerli ortak yapımcı ya da hizmet sağlayan yerli yapımcı şirket tarafından yapılır.

sources.title: Kültür ve Turizm Bakanlığı Sinema Genel Müdürlüğü: Dizi Film Desteği
sources.said: Başvurular yurt dışında yayınlanan ve ülkemizin tanıtımına katkı sağlayan yerli dizi film bölümleri için; yurtdışında işaret, ses ve/veya görüntü nakline yarayan araçlarla umuma iletim hakkını elinde bulunduran gerçek veya tüzel kişiler tarafından yapılır. Dizi filmin en az üç kıtada, on ülkeye ihraç edilmesi gereklidir. Destek başvurusunda bulunulan her bir bölümün ilk gösteriminin başvuru tarihinden önce en fazla 3 yıl içerisinde Türkiye’de, kablo, uydu ve karasal ortamlarda yayın yapan televizyon kanallarında gerçekleştirilmiş olması gerekmektedir. … 2026 Yılı Dizi Film Desteği başvurularının 02 Kasım 2026 Pazartesi mesai saati bitiminden önce eksiksiz olarak tamamlanması gerekmektedir.

sources.title: Mevzuat Bilgi Sistemi: Law No. 5225 Kültür Yatırımları ve Girişimlerini Teşvik Kanunu (RG 21/7/2004, 25529), consolidated
sources.said: Madde 4- … b) Kütüphane, arşiv, müze, sanat galerisi, sanat atölyesi, film platosu, sanatsal tasarım ünitesi, sanat stüdyosu ile sinema, tiyatro, opera, bale, konser ve benzeri kültürel ve sanatsal etkinliklerin ya da ürünlerin yapıldığı, üretildiği veya sergilendiği mekânlar … yapımı, onarımı veya işletilmesi. … Madde 5- … b) Gelir vergisi stopajı indirimi; … işçilerin ücretleri üzerinden hesaplanan gelir vergisinin, yatırım aşamasında üç yılı aşmamak kaydıyla % 50'si, işletme aşamasında ise yedi yılı aşmamak kaydıyla % 25'i, verilecek muhtasar beyanname üzerinden tahakkuk eden vergiden terkin edilir. … c) Sigorta primi işveren paylarında indirim; … yatırım aşamasında üç yılı aşmamak şartıyla % 50'si, işletme aşamasında ise yedi yılı aşmamak şartıyla % 25'i, Hazinece karşılanır. … d) Su bedeli indirimi ve enerji desteği; … elektrik enerjisi ve doğal gaz giderlerinin % 20'si beş yıl süreyle Hazinece karşılanır.

El programa está integrado por los aportes del Ministerio de Educación y Cultura, a través de ICAU - Instituto Nacional del Cine y el Audiovisual, y Televisión Nacional del Uruguay, el Ministerio de Industria, Energía y Minería, a través de la Dirección Nacional deTelecomunicaciones y Servicios de Comunicación Audiovisual (DINATEL), la Intendencia de Montevideo a través de Montevideo Audiovisual y TV CIUDAD.

sources.title: Convocatoria SeriesUy, Bases 2020-2021 (ICAU, Ministerio de Educación y Cultura)
sources.said: SeriesUy, llama a concurso de proyectos para la producción de una serie de ficción televisiva independiente. … Los proyectos presentados deberán asegurar la producción de una serie de al menos 180 minutos artísticos, de al menos 4 episodios de igual duración … Se adjudicará un único premio por la suma de hasta $5.000.000 (pesos uruguayos cinco millones) con destino a la producción integral de la serie. La serie premiada será emitida en los canales públicos Televisión Nacional de Uruguay y TV Ciudad.

sources.title: Kosovo Cinematography Center (QKK): Rebate
sources.said: Support Type: Rebate - 30% … Application Deadline: Open year-round … The rebate for audiovisual productions is 30% of eligible expenses incurred in Kosovo. Projects that also receive public funding from the Republic of Kosovo can benefit from the rebate for expenses incurred entirely in the country. However, the total benefits (public funds + rebate) cannot exceed 50% of the total production budget. … Salaries and social contributions for local screenwriters, actors, and technical staff. … The applicant must have publicly released at least one (1) audiovisual project in the last three (3) years. The applicant must secure at least 50% of the production budget and 100% of the foreign investment in Kosovo. … Feature films, documentaries, animations, TV series, video games, or other similar audiovisual productions. … For long-format projects, the rebate can be divided into up to three (3) installments.

sources.title: Incentives for Audiovisual Productions (MaltaInvest.mt)
sources.said: Productions receive a minimum 30 per cent rebate on eligible expenses, which can increase to 35 per cent if Malta is portrayed as itself or if local facilities like the Malta Film Studios are used. Employing local crews can boost the rebate to 40 per cent, provided specific department targets are met. … Productions can claim 10 per cent of the rebate upon the start of shooting, typically receivable within four weeks. … Applications must be submitted 30 working days before shooting begins. … Foreign performers pay a 10 per cent withholding tax … While no cap exists on Below-the-Line (BTL) expenses, Above-the-Line (ATL) costs are capped at €5 million and must not exceed 30 per cent of the total eligible spend.

sought: How a producer's project in each of twenty markets beyond the UK reads its market's public fund, cap on public aid, production incentive, fee and overhead caps and release rate (research/sources/person/markets/producer-<CC>.json, R-5135 to R-5154; Telefilm's, the CNC's and Screen Australia's terms from R-4612).
why: Every rate, share, cap, sum and bound is the research's own, read at its place (tools/person/markets-producer/readings.json) or written in the reading and found standing in the figure; how they are applied to one project where the research gives a rule, not a project, is the game's reading, named here so the player is told it is the game's own. The world round (2026-11-01, every country beyond the first markets): The research gives each figure at its place; these are the game's own choices in reading them, told to the player as the game's (add to the existing entry, R-5231's value)

value.award: A fund's yes pays the most its terms allow for the budget (its share of the budget, at most its cap, or its fixed sum), held to what the market's cap on all public aid leaves after the credit; where the fund sets no share of its own (the CNC's avance, the FFA's jury fund) the aid cap alone bounds it; refused where the credit takes all the aid.
value.shares: The Netherlands Film Fund's award at the 42% its supported features of 2024 drew on average (as the BFI's 22%); Norway's at the market assessment's low level (50%, NOK 9.8m); Italy's at the first and second features' 40% to EUR 4m for every project; Japan's at the general grant (not the young-film-maker grant or the 30% certified uplift); Canada's Telefilm at its English low-budget stream's 11.1% for every budget and its cap for languages other than French (the market's language is English).
value.credit: The incentive counts the whole budget as qualifying spend in the market except where the research gives the share counted (France and the Netherlands, 80%); a threshold on spend is read on the budget; Korea at a small company's base 15% (not the further 15%); Ireland at Section 481's 32% (not the Scéal uplift); France at the French-language film's 30% (the market's language); the United States at California's independent-film credit (Los Angeles is the market's city).
value.fees: The fee and overheads at each cap a funder sets, read on the budget: Germany's fee net of its own 5% as the research's example counts it (EUR 3.25m, EUR 154,375); Ireland's 15% (eligible spend over 80%); the Netherlands' 17.5% together under EUR 750,000; where a market sets none, no fee is carried.
value.release: Italy's 82% of the year's classified films reaching cinemas read as a project's chance of a cinema release, moved by the film and its campaign as the BFI's are; earning back twice the budget is told only in the UK.
value.shared: The option is the WGA's in every market; the market's money is sought in the EAO's shares and the producer's own 18% (European films') in every market; a market's months run in its city's zone as the actor's market there keeps it.
value.zone: A market's months run in the actor's market city's zone where the actor's engine keeps a market there (or its own three agreements); else in the zone of the country's most populous place on the map (GeoNames, first of the most populous in the gazetteer's file); none (refused at option) where the map has no place: BV, HM, UM. Needed because the actor's readings leave many countries unread (no zone).
value.currency: A market's currency is its country's (the gazetteer's) unless every term the engine reads is in another: AE, DO, JO, MN, MU, TT in USD; MD, MK, RO, RS in EUR.
value.spendIsBudget: An incentive's base (spend in the country) is read as the budget, as the twenty's are: the project is made in the market.
value.baseRate: Where a rate rises by points, bonuses or uplifts, the base (standard, minimum) rate is read: AE 35%, AM 25%, MT 30%, MU 30%, GE 20%, HR 25%, MD 25%, RS 25%/30%, TH, JO's third tier 35% (its 35-45%), PT's rebate 25%.
value.tiersNotBands: JO's and TH's rates by spend are read as tiers (the whole spend at the rate its level sets), not bands.
value.localProducer: Where a threshold differs for a local and a foreign production, the local's: MU's USD 50,000, TT's local 35% on US$15,000 to 8m; PL's feature (co-)production's over PLN 4m, not the service production's PLN 1m; CH's majority fiction CHF 1.2m; CO's CINA (35%, COP 3,151,629,000) and not the Fondo Fílmico (two rates by kind of spend). The CINA is a foreign production's alone, so since 2026-11-04 it isn't paid to a Colombian's film at home (foreignOnly).
value.portugal: Portugal: the Cash Rebate (25% from EUR 500,000 to EUR 1.5m) below EUR 2.5m, the Cash Refund (30% of the first EUR 2m, 25% above, to EUR 6m) from it, the two not combinable and the refund the greater.
value.panama: Panama's 15% to productions spending more than B/.3m up to B/.40m: none beyond B/.40m.
value.moldovaRelease: Moldova's release rate: 50 released of the 62 finished of the 102 projects backed 2017-2024 (a film released is one finished).
value.sloveniaRate: Slovenia's fund rate: 14 funded of 37 eligible in the 2026 fiction production call (features and shorts together).
value.austriaFees: Austria's fee and overheads caps read from EUR 2.5m (5% and 7.5%, to EUR 250,000 and EUR 375,000); below it the ÖFI's table gives single rows, not a rule, so no cap is carried there.
value.fundMostOnly: A fund's award given only as a most (Slovenia's EUR 1m, Senegal's CFA 150m) is awarded at that most, held to the cap on all public aid where there is one.
value.foreignOnly: An incentive whose own terms pay it only to a production from abroad (or a co-production with a foreign partner) is held so where a primary source of its figure says it (tools/person/markets-producer/readings.json names the words): Azerbaijan, Colombia, Estonia, Greenland, Latvia, Montenegro, Mongolia, Panama, the Philippines and Taiwan. The production company is the life's own, in the country of its first citizenship, so a film it makes there isn't foreign and is refused the incentive (told, producing.abroad); one it makes in another country is foreign there. The game makes no co-production, so an incentive open to co-productions isn't paid at home either. A territory's incentive counts a production from its sovereign's country as foreign (the game's reading: a Dane's film in Greenland is foreign there). Read on 2026-11-04; until then no limit was read and every such incentive was paid at home too.
value.seriesAndStage: A series' and a play's research beyond the UK (tvstage-<CC>.json) is read as a film's is: an incentive counts the whole budget as spent in the market except where its research gives the share counted; a threshold or a cap set by the episode, the hour or the minute is read on the budget of each, an episode's length being its running time where the series names one, else its slot's (60 or 30 minutes); where a series' terms are set apart for drama, documentary and animation, the drama's are held (every series the game makes is scripted); where one of two tests suffices (Germany's EUR 30,000 a minute, or EUR 1.2m an episode with EUR 7.2m a season), the first is held; a cap a law sets on a taxpayer's credits in a year (Spain's theatre credit, EUR 500,000) is held for each play, as the UK's Theatre Tax Relief cap is; an incentive whose own words take only a production from abroad, or one with a foreign partner or international financing (Buenos Aires City's 45%), is refused to the life's company at home, as a film's is; a territory whose research follows another's law (Christmas Island, Norfolk Island: Australia's; Réunion, Mayotte: France's; the BES islands: the Netherlands' High-End Series incentive, which names them) holds that market's figures with their sources; a fund's yes pays the most its terms allow; who may apply (citizenship, a non-profit, a company registered there) isn't checked, as a film's fund's isn't. No market's research counts how often a series is picked up or a run earns back its cost, so both are the game's own in every market (producing.model).
